collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE I: SONGS, CHANTS, SPEECHES AND WELCOMES (LCA-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola sings, chants and speaks for itself: welcoming a new leader, wishing travelers luck, greeting newcomers and newborns, rallying for hard work, standing up for each other, and arguing about who gets the next verse.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A new family has arrived on Isola: teach them the village's welcome song, or ask them to share one of their own.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A family has come to Isola from somewhere across the water, tired and very quiet, with a canoe full of everything they own. (subject) wants the village to welcome them properly. (friend) has already decided the new family's little ones are (friend.his/her) friends and keeps waving at them from behind a tree. What kind of welcome should they give?

choices.label: Ask for One of Their Songs

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The whole village gathers on the beach and sings the welcome song. The new family stands very still, unsure what to do with their hands. Then (friend) runs over and starts teaching their children the actions, one wave at a time. By the second chorus the newcomers are clapping along, a beat behind and grinning.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) asks the family if they have a song of their own. After a long pause, the oldest of them begins to sing, softly, in words nobody on Isola knows. The village listens in silence. When it ends, (friend) asks if (friend.he/she) can learn it. The family looks at each other, and for the first time since they landed, they smile.
